newsitem.title: JAPAN: DOLLAR SEEN FINDING SUPPORT VERSUS YEN IN ASIA.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR SEEN FINDING SUPPORT VERSUS YEN IN ASIA.

text.p: The dollar is likely to be supported against the yen around 114.20 yen in Asia on Monday after a nearly four-yen fall overseas on Friday compounded by a heavy sell-off in U.S. stocks and bonds, dealers said.
Japanese investors and some importers are likely to step in to buy dollars, but it could be difficult for the dollar to stage a quick recovery to 116 yen today, they said.

"Buying interest could be strong in Tokyo after the unexpected fall overseas," said a trust bank dealer. "But it will take time (for the dollar) to find clear direction, since the correction was fairly big," he added.
The trust bank dealer said further dollar selling would not be justified, with economic fundamentals still favouring dollar buying against the yen.
He said position squaring by overseas funds was responsible for the dollar's heavy losses on Friday.

"Many Japanese exporters, who will be on holiday this week, are unlikely to sell dollars at the current level," he said. Meanwhile, trust banks are also unlikely to conduct hedge sales for fear of a further dollar dive, he added.
He said the the dollar was likely to be capped at 115.80 yen before resuming its upward swing.

"It's unlikely that the dollar will fall below 114 yen," said a Japanese bank dealer. "But if it falls, that will bode ill for the dollar and a further decline to 110 yen cannot be ruled out in the near term," she said.
"If we can see the dollar recovering to 117 yen within a few days, the dollar will probably re-test 120 yen," she added.

Dealers said the dollar is also likely to be supported around 1.8420 marks. The mark was bought against the dollar after a Bundesbank official suggested on Friday that the central bank might raise interest rates to bolster the mark.
